headline_marked: LNG shortage: [[Gas supply cut to power plants]] to manage deficit
headline: LNG shortage: Gas supply cut to power plants to manage deficit
summary: Maintenance at a floating LNG terminal in Maheshkhali will lead to lower gas pressure for consumers over the next few days.
details: Gas supply across Bangladesh has decreased following the shutdown of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal for maintenance. The reduction in supply is expected to continue for approximately three to four days.
According to Petrobangla, total gas supply dropped from 254 crore cubic feet (ccf) at 8 AM to 208 ccf by 10 AM on Wednesday, a decrease of 46 ccf.
The supply cut is specifically due to maintenance work at the Summit floating LNG terminal in Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, which will remain closed from November 4 at 8 AM until November 7 at 4 PM.
Petrobangla has clarified that gas supply will not be completely shut off, but consumers may experience lower gas pressure during this period.
The authority has also dismissed rumors circulating on social media claiming that gas supply would be completely stopped for four consecutive days, calling it a deliberate attempt to create panic.
This development comes after significant gas shortages in August and September, which led to increased load shedding and hampered industrial production and domestic use.
caption:
Gas pressure may drop across the country as a major LNG terminal shuts down for maintenance.

Gas supply across Bangladesh has decreased following the shutdown of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal for maintenance. The reduction in supply is expected to continue for approximately three to four days.

According to Petrobangla, total gas supply dropped from 254 crore cubic feet (ccf) at 8 AM to 208 ccf by 10 AM on Wednesday, a decrease of 46 ccf.

The supply cut is specifically due to maintenance work at the Summit floating LNG terminal in Maheshkhali, Cox's Bazar, which will remain closed from November 4 at 8 AM until November 7 at 4 PM.

Petrobangla has clarified that gas supply will not be completely shut off, but consumers may experience lower gas pressure during this period.

The authority has also dismissed rumors circulating on social media claiming that gas supply would be completely stopped for four consecutive days, calling it a deliberate attempt to create panic.

This development comes after significant gas shortages in August and September, which led to increased load shedding and hampered industrial production and domestic use.

headline_marked: Video of [[man threatening others with pistols]] goes viral in Chattogram
headline: Video of man threatening others with pistols goes viral in Chattogram
summary: A man identified as 'Bullet Hridoy' allegedly displayed multiple firearms in a video, warning others to 'run while you still can'.
details: A 21-second video showing a man displaying several pistols on a cloth has gone viral on social media. In the clip, the man issues threats, telling others to 'mend their ways' and 'run while you still can'.
Police have identified the man as Hridoy, alias 'Bullet Hridoy', an associate of Mohammad Mamun from the Fazal Haque gang in Dakshin Raozan, Chattogram.

Hridoy is allegedly involved in extortion, mugging, and taking people hostage at gunpoint. Police suspect the firearms shown in the video may have been looted from police stations during the unrest following the fall of the Awami League government on August 5.
Assistant Superintendent of Police Balayet Hossain stated that authorities are verifying if the video is recent or old, but the police remain on high alert.
The region has seen significant violence since August 5, with law enforcement sources reporting 27 murders in Raozan alone.
Of these deaths, 20 were allegedly linked to political rivalries, primarily targeting members of the BNP and its affiliated organizations.
Additionally, over 100 incidents of gunfire and clashes have left more than 350 people injured in the area during the same period.
